A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dSVA research work. All 14 pages, including equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–E, are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original dSVA transferability experiments, parameter analyses, and ablations in Section 4, with additional cross-domain and defense results in Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–2 and 4–6 and the analyses in Figures 4–8.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same generator, DINO/MAE feature-facet exploitation, attention-saliency regularization, joint objective, and inference procedure. No method component changes.

E1.justification: Both use ImageNet and the same cross-domain datasets: CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN, STL-10, CUB-200-2011, Stanford Cars, and FGVC Aircraft. The defended-model evaluation scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 6 retain the same CDA, BIA, MI-FGSM, PNA, TGR, and ATT comparator configurations. Tables 4–5 retain the same CDA and BIA comparisons.

E3.justification: The ImageNet training set, 1,000-image evaluation set, fooling-rate metric, model configurations, and training budgets match. The perturbation bounds remain 10 for the main comparisons and 16 for Appendix C.

E4.justification: Both retain the same facet, layer, and joint-weight sensitivity analyses; self-supervision and attention ablations; feature visualizations; and defense evaluations. Appendix D also contains the same adversarial examples.

E5.justification: The aggregation descriptions in Sections 4.4 and 4.6 and the error bars in Figure 8 are unchanged. No seed information, repeated-run counts, or statistical testing procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical table entries and plotted results match, including the appendices. For example, Table 1 retains dSVA (Joint)'s 95.32% on Eff-B0 and 85.38% on Mixer; Table 6 retains dSVA (DINO)'s 20.88% on Res-18.

T1.justification: The threat model, feature definitions, attention-map construction, and mathematical objectives in Equations (1)–(7) are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises a theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and transferability claims concerning facet-level features, attention regularization, and joint exploitation of contrastive learning and masked image modeling.

C2.justification: The explanations of structural/textural complementarity, parameter effects, and defense transferability are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same physical-world evaluation limitation and proposed future extensions.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A retain the same generator details, optimizer settings, hardware, batch sizes, and training times. The code-access URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 73 references and related-work discussion are retained, including the positioning relative to generative attacks and the rationale for using DINO rather than DINOv2.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin label changes from v1 dated 26 June 2025 to v2 dated 30 October 2025. The paper's wording, terminology, headings, and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: There are very small typesetting adjustments, notably slightly increased paragraph spacing in Appendix E. All nine figures and six tables retain their content, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: The complete comparison, including Appendices A–E, shows unchanged scientific content, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information. The updated version/date label and negligible spacing adjustments do not materially improve or diminish the paper's quality.
